narrative.overview: A quiet, warm, low-lit room where you go to read and judge work that was done elsewhere. The agent's output is the hero on the page; the application is the lamp and the desk, not the subject. Everything is rendered with native-iOS precision (the lineage is Things and Ivory), so the calm never reads as unfinished. The single soft lilac in the system is the reading lamp: it appears only where your attention currently rests. The surface is warm-dark and never black; depth is built from four tonal steps, not shadows. Monospace is reserved strictly for literal machine text so that 'this is the machine talking' is legible at a glance. This system rejects the generic developer-tool look: no default dev-tool blue, no neon hacker green-on-black, no enterprise-SaaS chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-dark, never black: a four-step tonal system anchored at warm char (#0a0706).
One accent, rationed: Lamplight Lilac (#edb2f1) for focus and active state only.
Flat by design: depth comes from tone, never from shadow.
The work unboxed: assistant output and diffs get the full canvas; only the user's own messages are contained.
Tactile but quiet motion: a single press-scale spring, no bounce.
Native posture: system type, platform gestures, safe-area aware, 44px touch targets.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Lamplight Lilac is reserved for focus and active/selected state. Never a button fill, never a heading color, never decoration.

rules.name: The Warm Char Rule
rules.body: Never #000 or #fff. The floor is Warm Char (#0a0706) and the ceiling is Warm Paper (#f6f0ef). Every neutral is tinted warm.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Truth Rule
rules.body: Monospace means literal machine text: code, diffs, tool names, addresses. Never UI chrome; never System sans for code.

rules.name: The Flat, Tonal Rule
rules.body: Never add a shadow to create depth. Move up the tonal ladder, or draw a hairline border.

dos: Do reserve Lamplight Lilac (#edb2f1) for focus rings and active/selected state. A handful of lit elements per screen, no more.
Do render assistant output and diffs unboxed and full-width; contain only the user's own messages.
Do build depth from the four warm tonal steps (#0a0706, #100c0c, #191514, #221e1d), reaching for a hairline border before anything heavier.
Do use monospace strictly for literal machine text: code, diffs, tool names, server addresses.
Do give every interactive element the press-scale spring (to 0.97, no bounce) and a 44px touch target.
Do keep status meaning multi-channel: pair every status color with an icon or label.
Do keep body text at Ash (#c8c3c1) or lighter on dark surfaces so it clears 4.5:1 contrast.
donts: Don't use a border-left or border-right thicker than 1px as a colored accent stripe on list items or cards.
Don't fill primary buttons with the accent. Lilac is state, not a button color.
Don't use #fff or #000. Use Warm Paper (#f6f0ef) and Warm Char (#0a0706).
Don't put light text (#f6f0ef) on Interactive Gray (#969190); it fails AA. Use dark Warm Char text.
Don't reach for default dev-tool blue (VS Code / GitHub). Cobalt was retired on purpose.
Don't use neon hacker green-on-black. Greens are Muted Sage and Signal Green, never #00ff00.
Don't build enterprise-SaaS chrome: no nested cards, no dense dashboards, no busy toolbars.
Don't add drop shadows to fake elevation; move up the tonal ladder instead.
Don't default to a Modal. Prefer a bottom sheet or inline disclosure.
